documentation.content:
The daily credit-only roller (FC-078) either executed a roll or stranded a buy-to-close. The operator must KNOW either happened without reading logs.

Two conditions:
- call_roll_completed: both legs done. A short call was bought back and a higher strike further out was sold, at limit prices that netted a credit. This is the roller working. Informational, but it is a two-leg live order pair on the book — look at it the same day.
- call_roll_naked_exposure: the BTC filled and every STO ladder rung failed. The shares are UNCOVERED but long-only — there is NO naked short position. The residual is not a day of lost premium: worst case is the full BTC debit paid in cash with nothing sold against it, re-covered later through the entry path at entry-band premiums, adversely selected. Near a report the FC-013 span gate can legitimately hold the shares uncovered through the event.

Triage:
1. gcloud logging read 'jsonPayload.event_type="call_roll_completed" OR jsonPayload.event_type="call_roll_naked_exposure"' --limit=20 --freshness=1d
2. For a completed roll: confirm both fills in options_wheel.trades_from_activities after the next 15-min ingest, and that NO residual open order sits on either leg's symbol (cancel-then-verify worked). Assert new strike > old, new strike >= Alpaca avg_entry_price, fill credit = STO fill - BTC fill >= 0.
3. For naked exposure: confirm the next /scan -> /run re-covered. If the span gate is holding it uncovered through earnings, that is correct by doctrine — record it, do not override.
4. A repeated naked-exposure pattern is the thing to investigate, not any single instance.

Stop the roller without a deploy: gcloud run services update options-wheel-strategy --update-env-vars ROLLER_ENABLED=false (never --set-env-vars; it wipes the whole env set).

NOTE: the filter deliberately does NOT constrain severity. Cloud Run captures the app's stderr as plain text with EMPTY severity, so a severity>=WARNING clause matches nothing (FC-030 fire drill, 2026-07-18). Payload shape is matched both ways.

Rate limit is 300s, not the 86400s used elsewhere: a second roll on the same day is a separate event the operator must see, and the default suppression window would swallow it.

Plan: docs/plans/fc-078.md

conditions.displayName: Roll stranded a buy-to-close — shares uncovered

conditionMatchedLog.filter: resource.type="cloud_run_revision" AND resource.labels.service_name="options-wheel-strategy" AND (jsonPayload.error_type="call_roll_naked_exposure" OR jsonPayload.event_type="call_roll_naked_exposure" OR textPayload:"call_roll_naked_exposure")
